public_rationale: The cited papers measure exposure, not reliable task completion. Later evidence cuts in different directions: RLI finds very low end-to-end automation, while GPT-5.2 performs strongly on selected GDPval tasks. Neither supplies the representative occupational denominator and consistent reliability measure needed to establish or refute the broad claim. A citation mismatch alone does not prove the underlying claim false.
limitations: Digital projects and selected knowledge-work tasks do not represent every occupation.
Different task sizes and evaluation methods prevent direct comparison of the reported percentages.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Even state-of-the-art AI systems can reliably perform only a small fraction of tasks in typical human occupations.

statement.excerpt: At the task level, analyses of workplace automation show that even state-of-the-art systems can reliably perform only a small fraction of the tasks required in typical human occupations (Eloundou et al., 2023; Felten et al., 2023), despite high scores on idealized benchmarks.
statement.document_title: Rumors of AGI’s arrival have been greatly exaggerated

from_speaker: tasks required in typical human occupations
Eloundou et al., 2023; Felten et al., 2023
our_interpretation: This describes capabilities at publication, rather than only the capabilities of models studied in 2023.
Because occupational evaluations have no common reporting quarter, the target period covers the latest evaluation cycle: 2025 through February 17, 2026.
Reliably perform means complete tasks to an acceptable professional standard with consistent success, rather than merely assist workers or potentially shorten task duration.
Small fraction means a clearly small minority. No numerical cutoff is supplied or imposed.
Typical occupations requires coverage representative of occupational tasks, rather than only selected digital projects.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of contemporary frontier systems show reliable completion of only a small share of occupational tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show reliable completion of a broad share of occupational tasks inconsistent with a small minority.

evidence.explanation: The cited paper estimates exposure, including potential assistance. It does not measure reliable completion by systems current in February 2026.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Ed Felten, Manav Raj and Robert Seamans
evidence.explanation: The methodology deliberately leaves open whether exposure produces augmentation or substitution. It cannot establish a fraction of tasks reliably performed by contemporary systems.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Remote Labor Index research team
evidence.explanation: This supports limited end-to-end automation on the sampled remote-work projects. Those projects do not provide a representative denominator for all tasks in typical occupations.

This challenges a blanket characterization of poor professional-task performance. A win-or-tie rate on selected, well-specified knowledge-work tasks is not a representative occupational completion rate or a repeated-reliability measure.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative, occupationally weighted evaluation of systems available at publication, measuring repeated completion to professional standards under a specified level of human assistance.
